_comment: Invrisil 8c Task C3 (issue #13) -- Master Coyle's full quest graph: per-path confrontation + the expose-vs-extort epilogue fork (locked shape 5, both drafted endings shipped, real choice, both opaque-safe, NO default). Lifted from docs/design/dialogue-drafts/invrisil/merchant_prince.json with two changes: (1) accomplishment names NORMALIZED to the plan's literal locked shape 5 wording -- `merchant_exposed`/`merchant_extorted` (the draft used `exposed_merchant_prince`/`extorted_merchant_prince`; see invrisil_wilovan.json's own _comment for the same rename, kept consistent across both files so a save/gate check never has to know two names for one flag). (2) the accusation node's '(Draw steel.)' start_combat target changed from the draft's placeholder `merchant_blades` to the REAL locked entity id `hired_blades` (data/skeleton_scene.json, mercantile_alleys) -- C2's combat data + arena already ship under that id; this is the only entity id that exists. Voice contract: character-profiles-staging.md 'The merchant-prince' (prices everything including people, never raises his voice, flattery as a weapon). Speaker 'Master Coyle' = ORIGINAL+flag. `cornered`'s two ending options are the fork itself: EXPOSE (`merchant_exposed`, no gold, Coyle's one flash of self-awareness) vs EXTORT (`merchant_extorted`, +40 gold -- the SAME 40 gold his own ledger shows him paying the removal-man, the extortion re-pricing his crime at cost). Both ALSO bank the shared `merchant_fate_decided` convergence counter (the quest's 'resolve' beat, read identically regardless of which fork fired) -- `brothers_marker`/the safe-passage `remove_entity` reward live on Wilovan's side (invrisil_wilovan.json's report option), not duplicated here, since that is the genuinely shared 'quest complete' moment across all 3 paths and both forks. `cornered` has NO exit option BY DESIGN (you don't get to un-corner a man like Coyle) -- both its options are fully ungated, satisfying the softlock guard without an added back-out.

hub.speaker: Master Coyle
hub.text: A new face. I do like a new face — they're cheap, and occasionally they appreciate into something useful. Browsing, or selling?

text_variants.text: Come to inventory the wreckage? The Guild took the charter, the criers took the rest. I hope the hat-people paid you in something that keeps.
Ah. My consultant. Your retainer is current, your silence is appreciated, and my door — regrettably — is always open to you. Wine?

options.text: You framed a man for your own commission.
Your blades are groaning on a warehouse floor. Say it plainly this time.

accusation.speaker: Master Coyle
accusation.text: Do you know what reputation costs in this city? More than you. Considerably more than him. Whoever sold you that story overvalued your discretion and undervalued mine — an amateur's pricing error on both counts. So. Prove it, or price your next words very carefully.

options.text: Your own ledger prices it. Forty gold to a 'removal man' — dated the night before your theft.
Cups will swear to the hiring. So will Hellam — you soured his lease, and he kept the receipts.
(Draw steel.) Then we'll price it in teeth.

cornered.speaker: Master Coyle
cornered.text: ...Sit down. Please. Let us speak as adults who know what things cost. Yes — I paid for the removal; the frame was simply cheaper than the fee. Farley's sort are priced by the dozen. Men like me are priced by the CITY, and the city hasn't finished paying. So: name yours. Everyone has one. I find them all reasonable, eventually.

text_variants.text: Enough. ENOUGH. You've made your point in bruises, which is a currency I accept but do not respect. Yes — I paid for the removal, and the frame was cheaper than the fee. There. Plain. Now sit down and let us discuss what your silence costs, because everything costs, and you've just demonstrated you know it.

options.text: Not for sale. The ledger goes to the Watch, the Guild, and every crier with working lungs.
Forty gold — the removal-man's rate. A retainer, and Farley's charges evaporate by morning.

ending_exposed.speaker: Master Coyle
ending_exposed.text: Wait— ...No. No, you actually mean it. You held a fortune in your hand just now and you're going to BURN it — for a man in a cheap hat you've never shared a drink with. ...He'd say that's the difference between us, your Mister Farley. The tedious thing is that he'd be right. Get out. Go be expensive somewhere else.

options.text: The criers will explain the rest.

ending_extorted.speaker: Master Coyle
ending_extorted.text: Forty. ...Done — and worth it, which annoys me more than the sum. The charges were always mine to un-make; watch how fast this city forgets a theft once a rich man yawns. A genuine pleasure, consultant. I prefer enemies with prices. Friends run so very much dearer.
